analysis:
These changes touch only the advisory threat-review CI tooling under .github/scripts/threat_review, not provider or coordinator code. I mapped no retained provider threat (T-041, TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, A-015 to A-017) to a changed behavior. I checked the tooling for integrity of the review and clearance gate and for availability.

budget_scan.py: Validation now checks the needs_deeper_review type before acknowledgment and analysis. repair_response (lines 183-227) allows at most one extra paid call per scan. It applies only to BATCH_ANALYSIS_INVALID or BATCH_ACKNOWLEDGMENT_INVALID, and only after validate_findings has already passed on the first response. Transport, JSON, shape and cached-invalid failures are not repaired. Findings from the first response are retained through retain() before the repair call. Merged findings are the union of both responses, and needs_deeper_review is the OR of both, so a repair cannot dismiss earlier findings or uncertainty. The corrected response goes through the same validate() citation and acknowledgment checks. halt_if_stopped() runs before the repair call and after the checkpoint, so the budget stop is honored. A failed repair is marked failed and the exception propagates, so no retry loop exists. The integration schema constrains covered_units to an enum, and the cache identity now uses the per-stage schema, so cached entries do not collide across schemas.

budget_runner.py: alive() now fails on a closed or merged PR with a specific diagnostic. ResultWriteFailure blocks automatic clearance when the result file cannot be written. The status body shows repair counts and keeps the existing clearance conditions: complete coverage, no errors, no depth batches pending. The repair status does not weaken them.

diagnostics.py: Adds response_repairs to the diagnostics file, which holds metadata only.

Remaining unverified, outside the supplied evidence: the implementations of paid.stop_diagnostic, failure_record and the ReviewFailure.diagnostic shape, and how ResultWriteFailure is consumed by the CLI and workflow. I found no concrete regression.
